themes_detail.label: Electrical hazards spike
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints surged to 4 reports THIS WEEK versus 0.4 weekly average over 8 weeks (900% spike, z-score 7.49), with an additional spike of 14 complaints 2 weeks ago (220% above baseline)—signaling either a widespread infrastructure problem or a concentrated hazard zone requiring immediate investigation.
evidence: 4 electrical complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 7.49)
14 electrical complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 4.4 weekly average (z-score: 6.44)
Two-week pattern suggests sustained or recurring issue rather than isolated incident
reporting_angles: Investigate whether complaints cluster geographically—could indicate aging wiring, utility infrastructure failure, or construction-related damage
Interview Con Edison about service disruptions, downed lines, or maintenance work in Bay Ridge this week

themes_detail.label: Dead animal cleanup backlog
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints jumped to 17 THIS LAST WEEK versus 2.0 weekly average (750% spike, z-score 7.5), suggesting either wildlife issues, sanitation service delays, or seasonal die-off requiring rapid response.
evidence: 17 dead animal complaints last week vs. 2.0 weekly average (z-score: 7.5)
Sustained spike suggests systemic issue—not random occurrences
Aligns with CB budget request for garbage collection and recycling infrastructure improvements
reporting_angles: Contact Sanitation Department to determine response time and whether they're understaffed or overwhelmed
Investigate whether complaints cluster in parks (Fort Hamilton Parkway area) or residential streets—could indicate wildlife encroachment or seasonal factors

themes_detail.label: Fireworks complaints explode
themes_detail.summary: Illegal fireworks complaints spiked to 21 two weeks ago versus 0.9 weekly average (2300% increase, z-score 19.11)—the highest-severity statistical anomaly in the dataset, though timing suggests possible holiday-driven surge rather than ongoing crisis.
evidence: 21 illegal fireworks complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.9 weekly average (z-score: 19.11, highest z-score in dataset)
Likely tied to holiday period (Independence Day timeframe), but warrants confirmation of whether activity has subsided
No current-week data provided—need to verify if spike has resolved or continues
reporting_angles: Clarify timing: determine if spike was July 4th-related or if illegal fireworks continue THIS WEEK—critical for assessing ongoing threat
Interview NYPD 62nd Precinct about enforcement actions, complaint response times, and whether specific blocks are hotspots

themes_detail.label: Noise complaints surge
themes_detail.summary: Residential noise complaints jumped to 34 last week versus 11.4 weekly average (199% spike, z-score 6.91), indicating either increased nightlife/construction activity, inadequate enforcement, or seasonal behavioral change.
evidence: 34 noise complaints last week vs. 11.4 weekly average (z-score: 6.91)
Noise has been baseline 682 complaints over 90 days, but last week represented acute spike
No Reddit or news mentions suggest this is local knowledge not yet publicized
reporting_angles: Map noise complaint clusters by street and time of day—are they tied to specific venues, construction sites, or residential disputes?
Interview NYPD about noise enforcement capacity and whether Precinct 62 is understaffed relative to call volume

themes_detail.label: Street signs disappearing
themes_detail.summary: Missing street sign complaints spiked to 5 two weeks ago versus 0.8 weekly average (567% increase, z-score 6.43), a data-rich signal suggesting vandalism, deterioration, or DOT maintenance backlog.
evidence: 5 missing street sign complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 6.43)
Narrow, measurable problem with clear City responsibility (DOT)
Could indicate coordinated vandalism or systematic neglect in specific neighborhood zone
reporting_angles: Obtain missing street sign complaint locations from 311 database and map them—are they clustered (suggesting vandalism hotspot)?
Contact NYC DOT to determine cause (theft, weather damage, deferred maintenance) and repair timeline
